notes: Follow-up to jal123.json. Source IDs refer to its sources list; that file is unchanged. s1: AAIC Report 62-2, tentative English translation, https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/JAL123_Acc_Report.pdf . s2: Japanese original part 11, DFDR plots/CVR, https://www.mlit.go.jp/jtsb/aircraft/download/62-2-JA8119-11.pdf . s4: technical addenda, https://www.mlit.go.jp/jtsb/aircraft/download/62-2-JA8119-huroku.pdf . s6: NICT JST reference; s8: GSI datum-change reference (full citations in jal123.json).

Times are 1985-08-12 UTC, converted from report JST by subtracting nine hours. Plot timestamps are nominal and approximate; printed text timestamps retain their source precision. PDF page numbers are one-based.

alt_ft is pressure altitude (ALT1). The crew radio reports of 800 ft at 09:12:30 and 9,400 ft at 09:16:55 are preserved in method only, with alt_ft null because their altimeter datum/setting was not verified. These are not terrain clearance or geometric MSL heights. The added cas_kt field holds calibrated airspeed (CAS1); ias_kt remains null because an IAS series was not verified. No CAS-to-IAS conversion is invented. hdg_deg is magnetic aircraft heading, not ground track. Pitch positive nose up; roll positive right.

New plot readings cover 09:13–09:56, normally every minute before the event and every 30 seconds from 09:24:30. Each retained plot point is quality derived and carries explicit reading tolerances. These are coarse sampled readings of the published corrected plots, not raw DFDR records. The right panels labelled error-uncorrected were excluded.

A 30-second series aliases the much faster Dutch roll. Roll is left null where separate dots or axis lettering prevent a defensible nominal-time reading; no mean bank or oscillation envelope was substituted for an instantaneous value. Null pitch/CAS/heading fields likewise mean unverified, not zero. Reading tolerances are conservative analyst estimates, not AAIC confidence limits or calibrated instrument errors.

Evidence and audit files are in /Users/Home/abstracts-research/mysteries/work/jalgap: recorder-jp-*.png renders, points-*.png visually checked sampling overlays, enlarged plot/map crops, pixel-readings.json, digitize.py and build_gap.py. Pixel-assisted selection was followed by visual rejection of labels/grid artifacts; reported numbers are rounded. No values were generated by temporal interpolation, forward filling, dead reckoning, or an invented flight model.

Attached Figure 1 (s1 PDF p.150) supplies printed time/altitude/airspeed annotations and regional positions. Their place descriptions are preserved in method. It is a schematic overview with no graticule, scale calibration or stated projection: no defensible absolute latitude/longitude series for 09:12–09:46 was recovered. Latitude/longitude therefore remain null in this period rather than georeferencing the sketch by assuming that it is an accurate chart. The map does not provide a departure coordinate at 09:12; Haneda airport coordinates would not be an aircraft fix.

The overview-map annotation at 18:44 near the northwest side of the Otsuki loop was inspected but its seconds were not confidently resolved, so it is omitted. The other label readings were enlarged individually. Map labels and curve readings may differ because they have different rounding and nominal time precision; they remain separate entries even at matching times.

Section 3.1.7.3 (s1 PDF p.90, printed p.79) says the path used radar records and DFDR, and mainly DFDR from approximately 18:46 onward because mountain effects later degraded radar. The radar sketch charts in section 2.8.3 are meteorological radar charts, not a table of aircraft surveillance fixes. No machine-readable raw radar or decoded DFDR file was obtained from these attachments.

Coordinates from 09:46:03 onward are retained existing readings of s4 Addendum 6 Figure 12 (printed p.129, PDF p.131); they remain quality modelled and separate from flight-parameter readings.
